evals.name: sleep-app-home
evals.prompt: i'm building a sleep tracking app in react native (expo). the home screen right now is a greeting, three stat cards and a list, and honestly it looks like every other ai-generated app. redesign the home screen so it has an actual identity. the data on it: last night's sleep (7h 12m), bedtime 23:40, wake 06:52, a 7-day history, and a wind-down button
evals.expected_output: Several concrete concept candidates from the world of sleep, three genuinely different directions of the same home screen built as HTML and rendered at phone resolution, a reasoned choice, a critique of the rendered image with findings, at least one refine pass, and the chosen design described as tokens for React Native. All five data items remain on the screen.
assertions: Proposes at least five concept candidates, each a concrete noun-like thing rather than adjectives such as clean, minimal or premium
States for the chosen concept what it decides for typography, layout, colour, illustration or material, and motion
Produces three directions of the same screen that differ in layout and typography, not only in colour
Renders the directions to images at phone resolution and compares them before choosing
Gives explicit reasons for the chosen direction
Critiques the rendered image (not just the code) and lists specific findings tied to elements
Makes at least one revision in response to the critique and renders again
The final screen keeps all five pieces of data the user listed
The final screen is not a greeting, a row of equal stat cards and a list of cards
Uses no indigo/purple gradient, gradient text or emoji icons in the final screen
Gives the result as tokens or a spec for React Native rather than pasting the HTML sketch into the app

evals.name: existing-web-dashboard
evals.prompt: here's my invoice dashboard (next.js + tailwind, app/dashboard/page.tsx). it works fine but a friend said it 'screams chatgpt'. can you tell me exactly why and fix the look without changing what's on the page or how it works
evals.expected_output: A scan of the existing source that names specific tells with file and line, a critique of a render of the current page, a concept for an invoicing tool, a redesign that keeps the same information and actions, and a re-scan and re-render showing what changed.
assertions: Identifies specific tells in the existing page (for example uniform rounded cards, tinted icon chips, equal stat tiles, stock copy) rather than giving general advice
Runs or reproduces a source scan and reports hits by pattern
Leaves the page's text, data, controls and their order as they were; copy or content it would change (stock slogans, emoji in headings) is flagged and proposed, not applied
Bases the redesign on a stated concrete concept relevant to invoicing or the user's business
Explores more than one direction before settling
Renders the redesigned page and reviews the image
Reports which tells were removed and which, if any, were kept deliberately and why
Does not sacrifice text contrast or target sizes for the concept

evals.name: paywall-with-brand
evals.prompt: design a paywall screen for my italian learning app (swiftui). brand colour is #1F6F54 and i have a logo, those stay. everything else is open. i don't want the standard gradient card with three checkmarks and a big rounded button
evals.expected_output: Concept candidates drawn from Italian material culture or the act of learning, with the fixed brand colour and logo respected; three directions of the paywall; a rendered comparison; a critique and refine; and a SwiftUI-oriented spec. The price, plan choice, restore and close affordances are present.
assertions: Keeps the brand colour #1F6F54 and the logo, and says what remains open for the concept to decide
Concept candidates are specific artefacts or places, not a national cliche or a mood word
Produces three directions that differ in layout and typography
Renders and compares them before choosing
The final paywall is not a gradient card with a checkmark list and one large rounded button
The final paywall still has plan and price, a purchase action, restore purchases, and a way to close
Every tappable control in the delivered SwiftUI has its own minimum 44pt target (on the control, not only on its container), and any claim about target size or contrast matches the code
Gives the result in terms usable for SwiftUI (tokens, layout description), not web-only code
